clinician.trajectory_summary: 60-year-old Black African male presented with one-year history of progressive sinonasal symptoms (globalized headache, nasal obstruction, snoring, anosmia, epistaxis) and one-month left-sided visual loss. Physical examination revealed bilateral anosmia, severe left visual impairment (hand movement at 30 cm), and preserved right eye vision. Brain MRI demonstrated a T1 hypointense/T2 hyperintense anterior cranial fossa lesion arising from the left ethmoid and sphenoid sinuses compressing left optic structures, with CT showing heterogeneous masses. The patient underwent bifrontal craniotomy with extradural devascularization and gross total tumor excision with preservation of the optic nerve, chiasm, ICA, and pituitary infundibulum. Histopathology of the resected specimen revealed irregular tissue fragments with variable-sized glands lined by single to pseudostratified columnar cells with apical mucinous cytoplasm embedded in desmoplastic stroma, confirming the diagnosis of sinonasal intestinal mucinous type adenocarcinoma. Postoperative MRI confirmed gross total resection. The patient had an uneventful immediate postoperative course with GCS 15/15, resolution of behavioral changes by day 6, improvement in left eye vision to counting at 2 meters, resolution of epistaxis and nasal obstruction, and cessation of snoring, though anosmia persisted.
